Detective Samantha Cortez scanned the dimly lit apartment, her eyes narrowing as she took in every detail. The murder victim, a prominent tech CEO, lay sprawled on the floor, a single gunshot wound to the head. Cortez knelt beside the body, carefully examining the entry point and trajectory of the bullet.

"Hmm, based on the angle and lack of powder burns, this was a long-range shot. The killer was likely positioned somewhere outside, using a high-powered rifle with a sophisticated targeting system," she murmured, her voice barely above a whisper.

Cortez stood and began pacing the room, her gaze sweeping across the sparse furnishings. She paused in front of the large bay window, studying the glass for any signs of a sniper's perch. As she turned to continue her inspection, a faint shimmer in the corner of her eye caught her attention.

Cortez's hand instinctively went to her holster, her fingers curling around the grip of her plasma pistol. "I know you're here," she said, her voice calm and steady. "You can't hide from my cybernetically-enhanced visual sensors. Show yourself."

A figure materialized in the center of the room, the advanced cloaking technology fading to reveal a slim, athletic individual dressed in a form-fitting bodysuit. "Impressive, Detective Cortez," the killer said, a hint of amusement in their voice. "I should have known better than to try and evade your augmented senses."

Cortez leveled her weapon at the killer, her finger poised on the trigger. "It's over. You're under arrest for the murder of Dmitri Volkov."

The killer's lips curled into a smirk. "I'm afraid it's not that simple." They raised a hand, and a small drone emerged from the shadows, its targeting laser trained on Cortez's head. "You see, I've been monitoring your investigation every step of the way. And I'm not about to let you stop me now."

The airlock hissed as the prisoner was shoved inside, his magnetic boots clamping to the deck. Captain Yuri Volkov cycled the inner hatch, sealing them in the cramped interrogation chamber.

"You have one chance to explain yourself, Markovic," Volkov said, his voice clipped. "Why did you hack our navigation computer?"

Markovic sneered. "You know why. The Outer Colonies are tired of being exploited by the Consortium. We demand a fair share of the resources."

Volkov's eyes narrowed. "You sabotaged our FTL drive, crippling this entire mission. Do you have any idea the cascading effects that could have? The lives at stake?"

"Acceptable casualties," Markovic spat. "Your bloated empire will fall, one way or another."

Volkov's jaw tightened. "You're a terrorist, plain and simple. Our inertial dampeners are the only thing keeping your bones from being liquefied right now. So I'll ask you again - what is the override code?"

Markovic laughed mirthlessly. "Go to hell."

Volkov's gloved hand shot out, gripping Markovic's suit collar. "You have ten seconds before I vent this chamber. The override code. Now."

Markovic's eyes widened as the airlock warning lights began to flash. "Alright, alright! The code is 4-7-2-1-9-alpha!"

Volkov released him, tapping his comm. "Bridge, this is the Captain. I have the override. Restore FTL drive immediately."

Markovic slumped, defeated. Volkov fixed him with a cold stare. "You've condemned your own people, Markovic. I hope it was worth it."
